scope: My-Blog Original versus WeBridge latency experiment
source: Original public WeBridge JVM, runtime, synthesizer, JDBC driver, application and workload generator
workload_choice: Equal GI/BD/EB traffic, report each API separately; paper specifies equal probabilities for throughput, leaves latency driving mix unspecified
declared_repairs: Restore missing standard JDK build tools from pinned OpenJDK upstream
Repair stale package-name references; no optimizer transformation changes
Use direct supported GI/BD/EB API names in isolated driver copy
Save already-collected raw latency samples after timing ends
Use UTF-8 database default and procedure-installation client charset
Initialize offline connection pool before concolic replay
retained_artifact_behavior: Fourteen sample tag relations remain after population; missing relation addBatch is recorded and preserved

deployment.web_to_db: own Docker network namespace, database egress netem 2100us; measured ICMP mean2.145ms

paper_deployment_difference: Paper uses three separate eight-vCPU/16GB machines plus a separate offline compiler; CPU model, client-web RTT, process memory envelope and shared-host resources differ locally

measurements.latency: Original WeBench callback boundary includes HTTP response-body reading; raw nanoseconds and original quantiles archived
measurements.sql_census: Separate instrumented diagnostic; general_log top-level commands and independently cross-checked P_S nested events
measurements.pool_validation: SELECT 1 is counted and separately classified
measurements.formal_logging: general_log disabled and original P_S settings restored; per-request hit-rate logging disabled

comparison_boundary: Within-Java Original versus WeBridge on identical MySQL fixtures. Separate Jac/Java alignment is a correctness/query-count gate; cross-database absolute timings have different execution plans.
